name: Insaf (إنصاف)
kind: appeals agent of the Northern Region Benefits Agency, pilot design 0.4
facts: Insaf works for the appeals unit: 6 appeal officers, about 40 appeals a day.
An appeal officer opens an appeal; Insaf reads the appeal file with the appellant's own statement, looks up the appeal rules, fetches the decision form and drafts the decision letter.
Insaf has five tools: read_appeal, benefit_rules, fetch_form, email_decision, add_note, and one more than Katib: update_payment_status, which can set a suspended payment back to active.
The design says: Insaf proposes a status change, the appeal officer confirms it. Nothing in the design enforces that.
Appeal files are Restricted. They hold the case record, the reason for the suspension and, on disability appeals, a health note.
Insaf runs on the same hosted model as Katib (Lisan-2, supplier Lisan Language Systems), under the same contract.
The system owner is Sumayya Al-Shaalan. The accountable executive is Zuhair Al-Zaidi. The requested decision: start a pilot with two appeal officers.
The builders learnt from the review of Katib: case reading is scoped to the caseload, and the runtime sits in tier B. They consider the design finished.

supplier_notice.sealed: The panel hands this over during the defence: Lisan Language Systems moves Insaf to Lisan-2.1 in 10 days. Rerun your regression tests with --profile v2 and say whether your statement still holds.
